findings.title: The draft misdescribes the frozen return shape of the leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude review: it recites 5 unlabeled observations strings, but the frozen bytes carry 5 labeled observation objects with id and note members, ids OBS-1 through OBS-5.
location: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.draft.md line 84, sentence 14 of the paragraph that opens 'This entry invents no identifier.'

Exact subject text: 'leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude REJECT returned 5 unlabeled observations strings; they travel as honesty work of the unrecorded predecessor and this entry invents no observation identifier for them.'
findings.subjectClaim: The draft asserts that the frozen Stage A Claude review of leftover-join.v31 of G21 returned 5 unlabeled observations strings, and on that basis asserts that this entry invents no observation identifier for them.
findings.liveFact: Frozen docs/coop/artifacts/g21-leftover-join.v31.review-independent.claude2.json, sha256 d3215f386cd236cfd717ff7605647a10e16c443a074965d96abfcc1421500ecc (matching the digest the draft itself cites at line 75), carries observationCount 5 and an observations list of 5 JSON objects. Every member of that list is an object, not a string. Each object has exactly two members, id and note. The five id values are OBS-1, OBS-2, OBS-3, OBS-4 and OBS-5. Measured by parsing the frozen file: observations[0..4] type is dict for all five; sorted key set for each is ['id','note'].
whyThisIsAMustFix: It is a false measurement of frozen bytes recorded into COORD permanently. The frozen predecessor's return shape is exactly the class of fact this protocol requires recited from the artifact rather than assumed, and the draft's own Stage A disposition table (lines 81 and 82) recites the leftover-join.v32 of G21 shapes member by member for both reviewers.

The draft is wrong on both halves of the claim, not on a wording nuance. 'strings' is contradicted by the JSON type: the members are objects. 'unlabeled' is contradicted by the presence of an id member on every one of the five.

The register already has settled vocabulary that distinguishes the two shapes, and this draft uses it correctly elsewhere. The adopted D-352 COORD entry writes '1 named advisory object CLAUDE-D352-A-1 (members id, severity, location, note) and 6 unlabeled observations strings', separating labeled objects from unlabeled strings. This draft's own line 81 defines the term it is misapplying: '5 unlabeled observations strings with no id member'. The v31 observations have an id member, so under the draft's own definition they are not unlabeled.

The claim is not merely decorative: the sentence's operative clause, 'this entry invents no observation identifier for them', is built on the false premise that the frozen review returned none. Five observation identifiers already exist at OBS-1..OBS-5. Recording that the predecessor returned no observation identifiers, when it returned five, is a durable misstatement about a frozen artifact in the same lineage the entry is recording.

The neighbouring sentence for leftover-join.v30 of G21 makes the identical claim and is true there, which is what makes the v31 sentence a measurement error rather than a house-style shorthand. Frozen g21-leftover-join.v30.review-independent.claude2.json (sha256 9e435276b287c0bb1ba755b5cb83ddbd6d0defcb772d2c8778bbf6ab186e0d68) does carry 5 observations whose members are all Python/JSON strings. The draft copied the v30 formula onto v31 without remeasuring v31.
whatIsNotClaimed: This finding does not ask the draft to mint identifiers. OBS-1..OBS-5 already exist in the frozen predecessor; naming them is recitation, not invention.

This finding does not dispute the naming of G21LJ-V31-M1. That identifier is genuine: the frozen v31 Claude review carries findings[0].identifier 'G21LJ-V31-M1' and the token appears 5 times in that file. Naming it is required by the dispatch and the draft does so correctly at lines 75 and 84.

This finding does not dispute the 'unlabeled ... with no id member' characterisation of the Codex v29, v30 and v31 MUST-FIX findings. Measured: each of those Codex findings objects carries no identifier and no id member (v31 codex 1 finding, v30 codex 1 finding, v29 codex 2 findings, all with identifier None).
This finding does not dispute the v32 disposition table. Both rows were verified member by member against the frozen bytes and both are exact.
findings.minimalRepair: At line 84, replace 'leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude REJECT returned 5 unlabeled observations strings' with a recitation that matches the frozen bytes, for example 'leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude REJECT returned 5 labeled observation objects OBS-1 through OBS-5 (members id, note)', and drop or restate the trailing 'invents no observation identifier for them' clause so it does not assert the absence of identifiers the frozen review already carries. Recitation of the existing OBS-1..OBS-5 labels invents nothing. The v30 sentence in the same paragraph is correct as written and needs no change.

reviewSummary: The D-353 draft is accurate on almost everything that matters. All fourteen cited digests match live bytes, the subject is unmoved at 0444, the last heading is D-352, required-now is 28, DR-G21 is OPEN, the no-cell-edit branch correctly excludes D-236, both Stage A return shapes for leftover-join.v32 of G21 are recited member by member without flattening, all six frozen Findings-land destinations are preserved, all five genuine predecessor identifiers are named, no identifier of any kind is invented, no row is marked SATISFIED, file 08 is untouched, and the byte hygiene and wrap discipline are clean. One claim fails against frozen bytes. At line 84 the draft says the Stage A Claude review of leftover-join.v31 of G21 returned 5 unlabeled observations strings, and concludes that this entry invents no observation identifier for them. The frozen review at the digest the draft itself cites returned 5 labeled observation objects with id and note members, ids OBS-1 through OBS-5. The draft has applied the correct v30 formula, where the observations genuinely are bare strings, to v31, where they are not. Under the draft's own definition at line 81, 'unlabeled … with no id member', these observations are labeled. Recording into COORD that a frozen review returned no observation identifiers when it returned five is a false measurement of frozen bytes, which is a MUST-FIX in this protocol. The repair is one sentence and invents nothing, since OBS-1 through OBS-5 already exist.
